posts:
Federal land auctions ignite a high-stakes turf war as the Trump administration pushes geothermal leases over massive solar projects in Nevada.
Evidence: BLM lease auction, NextEra solar overlap, multiple-use mandate
#Energy #Nevada #Aletheia

The Trump administration argues that auctioning geothermal leases on public land promotes all-of-the-above energy independence through multiple-use management.
Stated Judgement: (+0.55, +0.10) — Greater Good

In practice, BLM auctions overlap 60% of NextEra's massive solar project, forcing rival renewable developers into high-stakes land conflicts without prior coordination.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.00, -0.35) — Greater Evil

Verdict: CONDITIONAL — Fall into Destruction.
Federal energy push collides head-on with private solar development, creating bureaucratic friction on public lands.
Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 2.5, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- BLM Land Policy: COND (+0.2, -0.3) — Pushes multiple-use without resolving prior land claims.
- Solar Developers: COND (-0.2, -0.4) — Faces land overlap risks on public leases.
The Bureau of Land Management is auctioning Nevada desert parcels for geothermal energy, directly conflicting with solar energy developments planned by NextEra and other giants.

The Poison:
Leasing disputed public acres first and forcing private entities to sort out overlapping claims later guarantees costly project delays and gridlock.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs WHERE plane error. Officials treat public acreage as blank slates on paper, ignoring the physical geography where solar panels and geothermal wells collide.

Social Physics Analysis:
The administration runs a top-down administrative push, overriding private project footprints under the banner of energy expansion. While not outright malicious, leaping to lease conflicting parcels without upfront grid coordination manufactures avoidable administrative gridlock.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When policy pretexts override spatial reality, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil friction. As administrative fiat collides with physical constraints, system strain multiplies.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public land multi-use mandates require harmonizing competing energy technologies before holding lease auctions.
The Unavoidable Lie: Forcing private developers to fight it out later is efficient energy planning.

Alethekanon:
Administrative efficiency is an illusion when official mandates ignore existing physical footprints. Bureaucratic fiat cannot legislate away spatial overlap.

Awwthekanon:
It's tough when big plans clash on the ground. Developers and regulators need to sit down and map things out so no one gets squeezed out unfairly.

Brothekanon:
Classic government move: selling tickets to the same seat twice and telling everyone to just work it out among yourselves. Good luck with that!

Spirithekanon:
"Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act." Proverbs 3:27 PASS
True stewardship requires order and fairness, not overlapping chaos that pits builders against builders.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump Admin’s Energy Plans Clash With Solar Giant

‘NextEra must collaborate with any potential lessee’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Mario Tama/Getty Images)

The Trump administration on Tuesday will auction off geothermal leases on Nevada desert land that solar developers want for their own projects.

NextEra Energy, a major solar developer, has asked the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to “remove, defer or reconfigure” three parcels that it said cover roughly 60 percent of the 1,000-megawatt Sawtooth solar project it plans in Nye County, Reuters reported Monday. The agency denied the request in August and pointed to its mandate to manage public land for multiple uses.

A geothermal lease does not authorize work that disturbs the land, an Interior Department spokesperson said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation. Developers would still have to submit exploration or construction plans for approval, including environmental reviews and consideration of other projects, the spokesperson said. (RELATED: Trump Officials Aren’t Waiting On Congress To Speed Up Permits For Pipelines And Power Lines)

Geothermal plants use heat beneath the ground to generate electricity and can operate around the clock, according to the Department of Energy.

Nevada’s October 2025 geothermal sale raised a record $9.4 million, with bids on 86 parcels, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said on X that month.

Alex Stevens, manager of policy and communications at the free-market Institute for Energy Research, said that the BLM should settle competing development plans before leasing disputed land, in a statement to the DCNF.

NextEra did not respond to the DCNF’s request for comment.

“BLM should stop treating high-conflict parcels as blank acres that can be leased first and sorted out later,” Stevens said.

Stevens urged the agency to evaluate where projects could connect to the grid and how soon they could be built, among other factors. The bureau could change parcel boundaries, allow uses at different times or select a project with a realistic prospect of construction, he said.

Stanford University professor Roland Horne stated that sharing land can work, though a geothermal power plant needs space where solar panels cannot go, in a statement to the DCNF.

“It’s even quite feasible to have wind and solar farms with geothermal wells drilled underneath them, if the appropriate rights and leaseholders are in agreement,” Horne said.

If NextEra receives approval first, a geothermal developer would need to prevent impacts on the solar project or pay the company compensation, the BLM wrote in its response to public comments. “NextEra must collaborate with any potential lessee and adjust its operations accordingly to avoid land use conflicts,” the agency said. (RELATED: Tech Giant Wants To Power Massive Data Center With Geothermal Energy)

The BLM initially announced 83 parcels across 10 Nevada counties, then revised the acreage to about 265,155 in a September amendment. One parcel that overlaps the Sawtooth site no longer appears on the auction website, Reuters reported.

Invenergy’s planned 300-megawatt Nivloc project and Arevia Power’s 1,500-megawatt Gold Dust project also overlap proposed geothermal parcels, according to sale documents cited by Reuters. Leeward Renewable Energy identified about 735 acres where a geothermal parcel covers part of its proposed Lone Mountain solar farm in Esmeralda County, in comments to the bureau

Half of the money from bids, rents and royalties from Tuesday’s sale will go to Nevada, a quarter to the county where each lease sits and a quarter to the U.S. Treasury, according to the BLM.

Geothermal leases last 10 years initially and can be extended for active exploration, development or production, according to the agency’s Nevada program page.

Nevada has 28 geothermal plants that are running or authorized on land with a federal interest, with more than 950 megawatts of authorized capacity, according to the BLM.

President Donald Trump thanked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Monday for pledging to give his company’s stock to every child who is participating in the Trump Accounts retirement program.

“A BIG THANK YOU to our legendary friend, Elon Musk, for his incredible generosity in giving SpaceX Stock to millions of American children through TRUMP ACCOUNTS!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “This is exactly what was envisioned when we created TRUMP ACCOUNTS — Bringing together the GREAT PRIVATE SECTOR, Elon and so many more, to invest in our children, by far our greatest and most important asset, and give every American Child a piece of the American Dream.”

Trump renews push to rename New Mexico ‘New America,’ touts higher home values and incomes

President Trump urged New Mexico to rename itself "New America," claiming the change would boost home values and incomes, while taking a swipe at state elections.

Actual Article Body:

Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., discusses his Senate race as President Donald Trump heads to Kansas to campaign for him on 'America Reports.'

President Donald Trump is giving New Mexico another branding pitch, urging the state to swap "Mexico" for "America" and suggesting the change could boost everything from home values to state pride.

"New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America. We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"The name would add great value and prestige to the State! Home Values and Incomes would rise, and you would be even prouder while saluting our beautiful American Flag!"

The president also worked in a swipe at the state’s elections.

AFTER 'LAKE AMERICA,' TRUMP SUGGESTS A NEW NAME FOR THE STATE OF NEW MEXICO

President Donald Trump renewed his call to rename New Mexico "New America," suggesting the change would boost home values, incomes and state pride. (Robert Alexander/Archive Photos/Getty Images/Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Maybe even the Crooked Elections, that New Mexico is known for, would become honest again!" he wrote.

MAP IT: DOJ ILLEGAL VOTING CRACKDOWN SWEEPS 17 STATES AS RAZOR-THIN ELECTIONS FACE SCRUTINY

Trump offered no evidence in the post to support his election allegation or explain how a name change would increase property values and incomes.

The suggestion revives an idea Trump floated last month, when he shared a map showing "Mexico" crossed out in red and replaced with "America." The White House amplified that post on its official X account.

TRUMP TAUNTS CANADA ON RENAMING LAKE ONTARIO THE 'LAKE AMERICA' AMID RISING BORDER TRADE RIFT

President Donald Trump speaks as Interior Secretary Doug Burgum looks on next to a map of "Lake America" during an event in the Oval Office of the White House on Aug. 27, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America." (Getty Images)

Trump also pitched the change during remarks at the RNC Midterm Convention on Sept. 9, suggesting neighboring New Mexico become "New America" and claiming the idea was popular.

"You have a neighboring state, New Mexico. We think it should be called New America," Trump said. "I’ll tell you, the people love the idea."

"I don’t know about the radical left. I’m sure it doesn’t like it, but the people love it," he added.

New Mexico’s Democratic governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, pushed back at the time, telling Fox News Digital that the state’s name "isn’t up for debate — it’s been ours since before the United States existed."

She accused the White House of focusing on a distraction while her administration worked on child care, education, health care and housing.

NEW YORK GOV HOCHUL REJECTS TRUMP'S 'LAKE AMERICA' RENAMING WITH BLUNT MESSAGE

New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham previously said her state's name is not up for debate. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"While the White House wastes time coloring on maps, Nuevo México is busy doing the work," Lujan Grisham said last month.

Trump’s latest post calls for the state to change its name but does not lay out a formal process for doing so. New Mexico’s name is expressly written into Article I of its constitution, which states, "The name of this state is New Mexico."

HOUSE DEM DEBBIE DINGELL PLACES TRUMP'S LAKE ONTARIO NAME CHANGE IN THE CROSSHAIRS

The proposal follows Trump’s moves to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" for federal use and the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America."

Fox News Digital's Amanda Macias contributed to this report.
